title: Hearing live interaction on records
summary: The difference between live and mechanical recordings.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: You can sense where--which way it's been done. Obviously you more than a non musician or a musician who hasn't had studio experience. I'm sure it's very easy for you to tell something that's been done with everyone in the studio at once as opposed to overdubbing.
It's very easy to tell if you AB it with something that has a live thing about it, where they're truly interacting. If they're just reading notes
forget it, but if they really make music of what they're doing, then you can tell right away. It's rare in classical recordings too, where they're really on, where it sends you.
